messages.subject: [VOTE] Airflow Providers, release preparation date 2026-10-20
messages.body:
Hey all,

I have cut a new wave of 30 Airflow provider packages with release
preparation date 2026-10-20.

This email calls a vote on the release. The vote will remain open for at
least 72 hours and until at least three binding +1 votes have been
received. The exact UTC deadline will be filled in immediately before
sending.

This wave includes the SMTP email backend, Google cancellation fixes, Azure
durable execution, and OpenLineage query-lineage changes. The OpenLineage,
Databricks and Snowflake changelogs include significant migration guidance.

The release candidate artifacts are available at:
https://dist.apache.org/repos/dist/dev/airflow/providers/2026-10-20/

The full source archive is
apache_airflow_providers-2026-10-20-source.tar.gz. The provider sdists and
wheels are convenience distributions.

All artifacts were built from the signed wave tag providers/2026-10-20 at
commit 27b075b9488793c5e70987b97e12ab8acdd35de9.

The signing key fingerprint is:
98820F00E5CF086C8A784091740F4342F6ECB77C

Public keys:
https://dist.apache.org/repos/dist/release/airflow/KEYS

Testing status and contributor testing requests:
https://github.com/apache/airflow/issues/75332

Staging documentation:
https://airflow.staged.apache.org/docs/

PMC verification instructions:
https://github.com/apache/airflow/blob/main/dev/README_RELEASE_PROVIDERS.md#verify-the-release-candidate-by-pmc-members

Contributor verification instructions:
https://github.com/apache/airflow/blob/main/dev/README_RELEASE_PROVIDERS.md#verify-the-release-candidate-by-contributors

Please vote accordingly:

[ ] +1 approve
[ ] +0 no opinion
[ ] -1 disapprove with the reason

Only votes from PMC members are binding. Community members are encouraged
to test and vote with “non-binding”.

The PyPI release candidates are:

messages.subject: Re: [VOTE] Airflow Providers, release preparation date 2026-10-20
messages.body:
-1 for microsoft-azure 15.3.0rc1.

This change: https://github.com/apache/airflow/pull/75272 makes the
PowerBIDatasetRefreshOperator now start the dataset refresh from the worker
instead of the triggerer. Workers that had no network access to the Power
BI domain (like an air-gapped cluster) will fail on every run after the
upgrade.
Setting durable=False does not undo it, so there is no Dag level way out of
this situation.

There's a fix in the works - https://github.com/apache/airflow/pull/74675

Thanks & Regards,
Amogh Desai
